column1: # Curated SEC filer decisions for the MONEY layer, and the refusals.
# WHY TICKERS AND NOT CIKs
# A CIK is the identifier that matters, and it is NOT written here,
# because every CIK in this file would be one I typed from memory. The
# ingester resolves ticker -> CIK from EDGAR's own
# https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json and then confirms the
# company's name and SIC from its submissions file. Identity comes from
# the source, never from a guess.
# WHY A FILE AND NOT A TABLE
# Same reason as org_aliases.tsv: a curated judgement belongs where it
# shows up in a diff, not where it can be UPDATEd at 2am (AD-052).
# WHY NO NAME MATCHING
# EDGAR gives a stable numeric identifier. Matching company names to
# `organizations` is strictly worse than mapping a CIK by hand once --
# and 2026-10-12 spent most of a morning on what name matching costs
# (AD-108, AD-110). org_code is decided by a person who has read the
# survey output, never inferred.
# decision: pending -> --apply REFUSES the row. The survey has not been
#                      read and no org_code has been chosen yet.
#           match   -> write claims, link to org_code
#           claim   -> write claims with NO org_code. The company is a
#                      real filer whose money we want; `organizations`
#                      simply has no row for it, and AD-085 says the
#                      link is an attribute rather than a requirement.
#           refuse  -> no claims. Say why.
# Every ticker below is UNVERIFIED until `--survey` prints EDGAR's own
# name and SIC beside it. Tickers are easier to be right about than
# CIKs, which is the whole reason this column is tickers.
# DECISION `consume`, added 2026-10-19.
# Not a softer refusal - a different axis. The other four answer "is
# this part of the space industry". `consume` answers "does this
# business rest on something in orbit", which is the DEMAND side:
# Garmin needs GNSS it does not own, T-Mobile resells Starlink
# capacity, Qualcomm ships modems that talk to satellites.
# A consume row's revenue is NOT space revenue, and --apply therefore
# ingests `match` and `claim` only. Lockheed's revenue is money the
# space industry earned; Garmin's is money consumers paid for handheld
# receivers, of which some unknown fraction reflects the value of a
# space service. The two are not the same number and must not share a
# column.
# This category cannot be populated by an SIC scan: consumers are
# classified under THEIR OWN industry, so the nine in-scope codes only
# ever catch the few that sit in communications or navigation.
ticker
LMT
